memory_candidates: CSLib task 317: intFuel (Expansion.lean) is under-provisioned by a factor-of-2 in its exponent relative to intExpMeasure's actual initial value (intWork_init = 2*|intUniverse phi| - 1, not |U|). Verified via #eval. Fix: double intFuel's exponent, mirroring Modal-K's modalFuel pattern (FmpMeasure.lean:231-242 hexp/heq step) which already builds in this factor of 2.

When porting a Modal-K FmpMeasure-style termination measure to a new calculus, always cross-check the fuel definition's exponent against the ENTRY-POINT measure bound derivation (the hexp/heq step), not just the universe-length bound alone -- the entry measure's initial intWork value is typically ~2x the universe size (one term per exclusion list, both near-maximal at the start), so the fuel exponent must be pre-sized with that doubling built in from the start.
